provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Review of First Term
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to recall advanced styling techniques, explain basic skincare routines, and demonstrate proper use of beauty tools.

Introduction:
Last term we learned about advanced styling and basic skincare. Today we will review these important topics to strengthen our knowledge before moving forward.

Content:
Advanced styling includes techniques like roller setting, pin curls, and finger waves. Skincare involves cleansing, toning, and moisturizing. Remember to use products suitable for different skin types like oily, dry, or combination skin. Always clean your tools after each use to prevent infection.

Class activity:
Students will practice advanced styling techniques on mannequins and demonstrate proper skincare application steps.

Evaluation questions:
1. Name two advanced styling techniques.
2. What are the three basic steps of skincare?
3. Why is it important to clean beauty tools regularly?
4. How would you help a customer with oily skin?

Summary:
Reviewing these foundational skills will help us build confidence and competence in our beauty and cosmetology practice.

topics.title: Advanced Skin Treatment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain the process of steaming, demonstrate proper exfoliation techniques, and prepare herbal masks for different skin types.

Introduction:
We have learned basic skincare routines. Today we will explore more advanced treatments like steaming, exfoliation, and herbal masks that improve skin health.

Content:
Steaming opens pores and prepares skin for treatment. Use a steamer or hot towel for 5-10 minutes. Exfoliation removes dead skin cells using scrubs or enzymes. Herbal masks use natural ingredients like aloe vera for soothing, turmeric for brightening, or clay for detoxifying. Always perform patch tests before applying new treatments.

Class activity:
Students will prepare different herbal masks using natural ingredients and practice steaming and exfoliation techniques on classmates' arms.

Evaluation questions:
1. What is the purpose of steaming in skincare?
2. Name two natural ingredients used in herbal masks.
3. How long should you steam the face?
4. Why is patch testing important before skin treatments?

Summary:
These advanced treatments help address specific skin concerns and improve overall skin texture and appearance when done correctly.

topics.title: Makeup Products and Their Functions
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify different makeup products, explain their functions, and demonstrate proper application techniques.

Introduction:
We have studied skincare treatments. Now we will focus on makeup products and how each one helps to enhance beauty and correct imperfections.

Content:
Concealer covers blemishes and dark spots. Powder sets makeup and reduces shine. Lipstick adds color and defines lips. Eyeliner enhances eye shape and makes eyes appear larger. Apply makeup in the correct order: primer, foundation, concealer, powder, eye makeup, then lipstick. Remember to match products to the client's skin tone and occasion.

Class activity:
Students will practice applying different makeup products on each other, focusing on proper technique and product selection for different face shapes.

Evaluation questions:
1. What is the main function of concealer?
2. Name the correct order of makeup application.
3. How would you choose lipstick color for a client with dark skin?
4. Why is primer important before foundation?

Summary:
Understanding each makeup product's function and proper application technique is essential for creating beautiful, long-lasting looks.

topics.title: Hairdressing Tools
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify various hairdressing tools, explain their proper maintenance, and demonstrate correct usage techniques.

Introduction:
Last week we focused on makeup. Today we will learn about hairdressing tools, how to care for them, and their proper use in different hairstyling techniques.

Content:
Essential tools include scissors, clippers, combs, brushes, and rollers. Clean tools after each use with disinfectant solution. Store in a dry place to prevent rust. Sharpen scissors regularly for clean cuts. Check electrical tools for damaged cords before use. Proper maintenance ensures tools last longer and provide better results.

Class activity:
Students will practice different hairstyling techniques using the proper tools and demonstrate how to clean and maintain each tool correctly.

Evaluation questions:
1. Why is it important to disinfect hair tools after each use?
2. Name three essential hairdressing tools.
3. How should you store scissors to maintain their sharpness?
4. What should you check before using electrical hair tools?

Summary:
Proper care and maintenance of hairdressing tools is crucial for hygiene, safety, and achieving professional hairstyling results.

topics.title: Midterm Examination
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to demonstrate their understanding of the topics covered in the first half of the term.

Introduction:
We have learned about advanced skin treatment, makeup products, and hairdressing tools. Now it is time to assess your knowledge through the midterm examination.

Content:
The midterm examination will cover topics from week 1 to week 4. Review your notes on advanced styling, skincare treatments, makeup products and functions, and hairdressing tools. The exam will include multiple choice, short answer, and practical demonstration questions.

Class activity:
Students will complete the midterm examination which tests both theoretical knowledge and practical skills demonstrated on mannequins or classmates.

Evaluation questions:
The midterm examination will serve as the evaluation for this week.

Summary:
This assessment will help identify areas of strength and those needing improvement before we continue with the remaining topics.

topics.title: Customer Care
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to demonstrate effective communication skills, explain proper complaint handling procedures, and practice good customer service techniques.

Introduction:
After our midterm break, we will focus on customer care - an essential skill for any beauty professional working with clients in a salon setting.

Content:
Good communication includes active listening, clear speaking, and maintaining eye contact. Handle complaints by listening carefully, apologizing sincerely, offering solutions, and following up. Build rapport by remembering regular clients' preferences and names. Maintain professionalism by being punctual, dressed appropriately, and respecting client privacy. Always ask for feedback after services.

Class activity:
Students will role-play different customer service scenarios including handling difficult clients and practicing effective communication techniques.

Evaluation questions:
1. What are three important elements of good communication?
2. Describe the steps for handling a client complaint.
3. Why is it important to remember regular clients' preferences?
4. How would you respond if a client is unhappy with their hairstyle?

Summary:
Excellent customer care builds trust, encourages repeat business, and creates a positive reputation for your salon or beauty business.

topics.title: Midterm Break
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to rest and recharge for the second half of the term.

Introduction:
This is a midterm break to allow students and teachers to rest before continuing with the remaining topics in the term.

Content:
Use this break to rest, revise previously learned topics, and prepare for the second half of the term. Students are encouraged to observe beauty professionals in their communities to see how the concepts we've learned are applied in real salon settings.

Class activity:
No formal class activity during break period. Students are encouraged to practice skills learned in previous weeks and observe professional salons in their local areas.

Evaluation questions:
No formal evaluation during break period.

Summary:
Enjoy your break and return refreshed and ready to learn more about beauty and cosmetology.

topics.title: Professional Ethics
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain the importance of professional ethics in beauty practice, demonstrate honesty and confidentiality with client information, and maintain professional appearance and punctuality.

Introduction:
As we continue our beauty and cosmetology studies, it is important to understand the ethical standards that guide our profession and build trust with clients.

Content:
Professional ethics includes honesty in service and pricing, maintaining neat appearance and clean workspace, being punctual for appointments, and keeping client information confidential. Always recommend services that benefit the client rather than just increasing sales. Respect cultural differences and personal boundaries. Admit mistakes and correct them promptly. Follow health and safety regulations strictly.

Class activity:
Students will create a code of ethics poster for a beauty salon and role-play scenarios demonstrating ethical dilemmas and their proper resolution.

Evaluation questions:
1. Why is confidentiality important in beauty services?
2. How would you handle a situation where a client asks for a service that isn't suitable for their needs?
3. What are three elements of professional appearance for a beauty therapist?
4. Why is honesty important in client relationships?

Summary:
Adhering to professional ethics builds trust, ensures quality service, and contributes to the positive reputation of the beauty industry.

topics.title: Entrepreneurship in Beauty
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify business opportunities in the beauty industry, outline steps to start a small salon, and explain basic principles of salon management.

Introduction:
After learning about professional ethics, we will now explore entrepreneurship in the beauty industry - how to turn your skills into a successful business venture.

Content:
Identify opportunities by researching local beauty needs and competition. Start small with home services or a small space before expanding. Develop a business plan including services offered, pricing, target market, and marketing strategy. Manage finances by keeping accurate records, separating business and personal accounts, and setting aside taxes. Build customer loyalty through quality service and loyalty programs.

Class activity:
Students will develop a simple business plan for a small beauty salon including service menu, pricing, and basic marketing strategy.

Evaluation questions:
1. What are three steps to identify business opportunities in beauty?
2. Why is it important to keep accurate financial records?
3. How would you market a new beauty salon in your local area?
4. What should be included in a basic business plan for a beauty salon?

Summary:
Entrepreneurial skills combined with beauty expertise can lead to successful and sustainable business ventures in the growing beauty industry.

topics.title: Record Keeping and Financial Management
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain the importance of record keeping, demonstrate basic bookkeeping techniques, and calculate appropriate pricing for beauty services.

Introduction:
Building on our entrepreneurship lesson, we will focus specifically on record keeping and financial management - essential skills for running a successful beauty business.

Content:
Maintain client records with contact details, service history, and preferences. Track income and expenses using simple books or digital apps. Create budgets by estimating monthly costs and revenue. Price services by calculating material costs, time required, and desired profit margin. Consider local market rates when setting prices. Keep financial records organized for tax purposes and business analysis.

Class activity:
Students will practice creating service price lists based on cost analysis and maintain sample client appointment books for a week.

Evaluation questions:
1. What information should be included in client records?
2. How do you calculate the price for a new beauty service?
3. Why is budgeting important for a small beauty business?
4. What are two methods for tracking income and expenses?

Summary:
Proper record keeping and financial management ensure business sustainability, profitability, and compliance with regulatory requirements.

topics.title: Revision
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to recall and explain key concepts from the term's topics and demonstrate practical skills learned throughout the term.

Introduction:
As we approach the end of the term, we will revise all the topics covered to reinforce learning and prepare for the final examination.

Content:
We will review advanced skin treatments, makeup products and functions, hairdressing tools, customer care, professional ethics, entrepreneurship, and record keeping. Focus on both theoretical understanding and practical application. Pay special attention to topics that were challenging during the midterm examination. Practice techniques that require manual skill development.

Class activity:
Students will participate in group revision sessions where they teach each other different concepts and practice practical skills on mannequins and with partners.

Evaluation questions:
1. Explain the process of steaming and exfoliation in skincare.
2. How would you handle a client complaint about a service?
3. What are the key elements of professional ethics in beauty practice?
4. How do you price a new beauty service appropriately?

Summary:
Thorough revision of all topics will help ensure comprehensive understanding and prepare students for successful completion of the term.

topics.title: Revision
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to demonstrate comprehensive knowledge of all term topics and apply skills in practical assessment situations.

Introduction:
Continuing our revision process, we will focus on reinforcing difficult concepts and practicing examination techniques to build confidence for the final assessment.

Content:
Focus on areas where students showed weakness during midterm and previous revision sessions. Practice time management for the examination format. Review case studies that combine multiple concepts. Prepare for both written and practical examination components. Ensure understanding of safety procedures and hygiene practices in all beauty services.

Class activity:
Students will complete mock examinations under timed conditions and participate in peer assessment of practical skills to identify areas for improvement.

Evaluation questions:
1. What are the steps to start a small beauty business?
2. How do you maintain professional ethics when dealing with difficult clients?
3. Explain the importance of proper tool maintenance in hairdressing.
4. How would you create a business plan for a beauty salon?

Summary:
This final revision will help students consolidate their learning and approach the end-of-term examination with confidence and preparedness.

topics.title: Examination / Closing
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to demonstrate comprehensive knowledge and skills acquired throughout the term in the final examination.

Introduction:
This week marks the end of the term with final examinations and closing activities to celebrate our learning journey in beauty and cosmetology.

Content:
The final examination will cover all topics studied during the term including theory and practical components. After the examination, we will have a closing session to reflect on what we have learned, set goals for the next term, and discuss career opportunities in the beauty industry. Certificates of participation will be awarded to all students.

Class activity:
Students will complete the final examination and participate in a closing ceremony where they demonstrate their favorite skills learned during the term.

Evaluation questions:
The final examination will serve as the evaluation for this week, testing both theoretical knowledge and practical skills.

Summary:
This concludes our beauty and cosmetology studies for the term. Congratulations on your hard work and dedication to developing professional skills in this exciting field.
